threat_scenario: Replay of a captured authentication code that the vehicle never received
attack_path: Attacker near the vehicle with a transmit/receive SDR; on the owner's lock press, jam the 433 MHz band and capture the code (vehicle receives nothing, stays unlocked); on the second press, jam+capture again and replay the first code (vehicle locks, owner leaves); replay the retained second code later, with its command field switched to unlock (A-10), to open the vehicle. The vehicle never received that code, so the stored counter never advanced past it; the retained code stays valid until the next legitimate press.
feasibility_rationale: Consumer SDR (e.g. HackRF, ~300EUR), technique published since 2015. Elapsed time: <=1 day. Specialist expertise: Proficient (jamming + capture + ordered replay). Knowledge of the item: Public (no item-specific information needed). Equipment: Specialized (transmit-capable SDR). Window of opportunity: Moderate (presence required at the lock press, and no legitimate press before the replay). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates High; the full 5-factor scoring planned for v0.3 may lower it.
assumptions: A-10 (command field not covered by the authentication code)

threat_scenario: Denial jamming: jam the 433 MHz band during the lock command so the BCM receives nothing and the vehicle stays unlocked while the owner believes it is locked
attack_path: Attacker positioned near a parked vehicle, within radio range (`01` §5), with an off-the-shelf 433 MHz jammer; when the owner presses the key-fob lock button, the attacker jams the band so the BCM receives no frame and the doors stay unlocked; the attack succeeds only if the owner leaves without checking the lock-confirmation feedback (no indicator flash is possible, since the BCM did not lock); the attacker then accesses the unlocked vehicle
feasibility_rationale: Opportunistic radio attack, no physical access. Elapsed time: low (immediate setup). Specialist expertise: Layman (the technique is widely documented). Knowledge of the item: Public (no information about this item is needed). Equipment: Standard (off-the-shelf 433 MHz jammer, simpler than the TS-01 SDR). Window of opportunity: Moderate (many lock events in a public car park, but each attempt needs the exact lock instant and an owner who does not verify the feedback). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates High; see the §4 scale limitation.

threat_scenario: Pair an attacker key via OBD diagnostic, then open the vehicle with it
attack_path: Attacker with temporary authorized access to the vehicle and its key fob (valet / rental / workshop); using an OBD-II diagnostic tool plugged into the in-cabin port (`01` A-03), the attacker invokes the key-pairing service F-03, routed through the gateway to the BCM (I-05 then I-04), and enrols an additional attacker-controlled key; the vehicle is returned, and the attacker later opens it at will with the enrolled key (persistent covert access)
feasibility_rationale: Temporary authorized access (valet / rental / workshop), limited physical access via the in-cabin OBD port (`01` A-03). Elapsed time: <=1 day (pairing is quick once access is obtained). Specialist expertise: Proficient (requires knowing the diagnostic key-pairing procedure). Knowledge of the item: Restricted (the pairing procedure is service/workshop-restricted, not public). Window of opportunity: Moderate (such access situations occur, but each attempt needs the attacker unobserved while connecting the tool and able to locate the vehicle again later). Equipment: Specialized (a diagnostic tool able to run the key-pairing routine). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Medium (OBD access inside the cabin).
assumptions: A-01 (gateway routes diagnostic requests to the BCM), A-03 (OBD port in the cabin)

threat_scenario: Pair an attacker key via direct CAN injection (exterior harness), bypassing the gateway, then open the vehicle with it
attack_path: Attacker with a low-cost CAN interface; locate an exterior connector that exposes body CAN (e.g. an adaptive-headlight ECU), remove the bodywork to reach it, and inject the F-03 pairing request directly to the BCM diagnostic endpoint on I-04, bypassing the gateway (I-07); an attacker-controlled key is enrolled and the vehicle is later opened with it (persistent covert access)
feasibility_rationale: Direct injection on body CAN via an exterior connector exposing a CAN node (e.g. an adaptive-headlight ECU), reaching the BCM diagnostic endpoint on I-04 and bypassing the gateway (I-07). Elapsed time: <=1 day (assuming the pairing procedure is known). Specialist expertise: Expert - the F-03 pairing frames are crafted directly in raw CAN/ISO-TP, without the workshop tool that frames them in TS-03. Knowledge of the item: Restricted - same service-restricted pairing procedure as TS-03. Equipment: Specialized (USB-CAN interface). Window of opportunity: Moderate - more available than TS-03 (no authorized access needed), but each attempt needs bodywork removed unobserved. By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Medium (exterior harness connector); Expert + Specialized would pull lower under a full 5-factor scoring, so this may drop to Low in v0.3.

threat_scenario: Extract K via key-fob debug interface during temporary possession, return the fob, then use the retained clone later to open the vehicle (valet/rental scenario)
attack_path: Attacker with temporary possession of the fob (valet / rental / workshop); opens the fob casing, connects to the chip debug interface (I-06a) and reads the key secret K from memory, returns the fob to the owner, and later fabricates a clone to open the vehicle (persistent covert access)
feasibility_rationale: Invasive physical access: opening the fob casing and probing the chip debug interface (I-06a). Elapsed time: <=1 day (fob in hand). Specialist expertise: Expert (open the device, read a protected MCU via debug). Knowledge of the item: Restricted (where K is stored in the fob). Equipment: Specialized (debug probe / chip tooling). Window of opportunity: Moderate (valet/rental possession). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Low (invasive physical access to a PCB debug interface).
assumptions: A-12 (no readout protection on the fob debug path I-06a)

asset: Key secrets stored in the BCM (all paired keys)
threat_scenario: Read all stored secrets via BCM debug interface, then clone a key and open the vehicle
attack_path: Attacker with prolonged unsupervised access to the vehicle; removes the BCM, solders onto its debug interface (I-06b) and dumps the non-volatile memory, obtaining the secrets of all paired keys; the dump is non-destructive (the keys remain in place); the attacker then clones any key and opens the vehicle
feasibility_rationale: Invasive physical access: removing the BCM and soldering onto its debug interface (I-06b). Elapsed time: <=1 day. Specialist expertise: Expert (desolder/solder, memory dump). Knowledge of the item: Restricted (BCM memory map). Equipment: Specialized (debug probe, soldering). Window of opportunity: Difficult (prolonged unsupervised access to remove and refit the BCM). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Low (invasive physical access).
assumptions: A-07 (no effective debug-access protection on I-06b)

threat_scenario: Roll the stored counter back via BCM debug, so a previously captured code becomes valid again and opens the vehicle
attack_path: Attacker with prolonged unsupervised access to the vehicle who has captured a valid code earlier by radio; removes the BCM, solders onto its debug interface (I-06b) and overwrites the stored rolling-code counter with a lower value, so the retained code is once again strictly greater than the stored counter; the BCM then accepts that code and the vehicle opens

Elapsed time: <=1 day. Specialist expertise: Expert (desolder/solder, NVM write). Knowledge of the item: Restricted (BCM memory map, counter location). Equipment: Specialized (debug probe, soldering). Window of opportunity: Difficult (prolonged unsupervised access). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Low (invasive physical access).
assumptions: A-07 (no effective debug-access protection on I-06b)

threat_scenario: Flash a backdoored firmware via the BCM debug interface, bypassing RKE authentication and enabling unauthorized door or trunk release
attack_path: Attacker with prolonged unsupervised access to the vehicle; removes the BCM, solders onto its debug interface (I-06b) and flashes a modified firmware that ignores the RKE authentication or carries a backdoor command; refitted, the BCM opens the vehicle on the attacker's command. The replaced firmware voids every software check at once (02_tara-method.md §9)
feasibility_rationale: Invasive physical access: removing the BCM and writing its program memory via the debug interface (I-06b). Elapsed time: <=1 day. Specialist expertise: Expert (desolder/solder, firmware build and flash). Knowledge of the item: Restricted (memory map, firmware format). Equipment: Specialized (debug probe, soldering). Window of opportunity: Difficult (prolonged unsupervised access). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Low (invasive physical access).
assumptions: A-07 (no effective debug-access protection on I-06b) and A-11 (no effective firmware authenticity or integrity protection)

asset: Correlatable radio emission (Key ID + rolling-code counter)
threat_scenario: Eavesdrop the Key ID and the clear-text rolling-code counter, both broadcast on every button press; correlate repeated captures to infer the owner's presence and habits
attack_path: Observer within radio range (`01` §5) with a receive-only SDR; logs the Key ID (A-06, stable) and the rolling-code counter, both sent in clear, the counter being monotonic so it links successive transmissions of one fob even if the identifier changes; correlating repeated captures over time reveals the owner's presence, absence and travel habits. No intrusion and no interaction with the vehicle
feasibility_rationale: Passive radio eavesdropping, no physical access and no interaction. Elapsed time: the capture is immediate; building a habits profile takes repeated observation. Specialist expertise: Layman (read a clear-text field). Knowledge of the item: Public (fields sent in clear, no item information needed). Equipment: Standard (receive-only SDR / RTL-SDR). Window of opportunity: Unlimited (every button press emits them). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates High (radio without intrusion).
